justification: Backend logic fix to the capacity engine's DCP control selection. A statewide read-only audit of dcp_setback_controls (28 LGAs, 1001 current rows) found 62 groups where more than one current row shares the same (control_type, dev_type) — 53 legitimately tiered (lot-size/storey/street bands, with conditions) and 9 unconditioned/suspect (e.g. Burwood front_setback 9m AND 15m, both mis-extracted from non-setback clauses P8/P39). _get_dcp_value matched on (control_type, dev_type) and kept the LAST row in iteration order, ignoring the condition field, so the chosen setback was arbitrary and order-dependent. This makes selection deterministic and conservative: max(value_min) for minimum-requirement controls (largest setback = smallest buildable envelope = fail-safe, never over-reports capacity) and min(value_max) for prefer_max caps (tightest allowance); single-row callers are byte-for-byte unchanged. It also surfaces a data-gap when it had to choose between conflicting setback values, so the figure reads as verify-against-DCP rather than a single certain control. Pure in-memory function; no DB query/schema/IO change. Tier-accurate matching (parsing lot size/width/storeys from condition) is a separate, larger follow-up.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls (1001 current rows, 28 LGAs) is the source; fetch_dcp_setbacks returns all current rows with no dedup and minimal zone filtering. Confirmed via read-only audit that multi-row (control_type, dev_type) groups are common (62) and that _get_dcp_value previously consumed only the last matching row.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed one DCP value per control; in reality controls are tiered or sometimes duplicated/garbled, so several rows match. The condition field that distinguishes tiers was being ignored entirely by the selector.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Extends the existing _get_dcp_value rather than adding a parallel path; adds two small pure helpers (_matching_controls, _dcp_value_conflict) reused by the selector and the gap-flagging. No new DB query or table introduced.

functions.name: _get_dcp_value
functions.input: a DCPControl list, a control_type string, a dev_type string, and an optional prefer_max flag for cap controls
functions.output: a single float chosen deterministically and conservatively across all matching rows (max value_min, or min value_max when prefer_max), or None when nothing matches
functions.if_none: returns None when no row matches the control_type for the exact dev_type or the dwelling_house fallback, exactly as before

functions.name: _matching_controls
functions.input: a DCPControl list, a control_type string and a dev_type string
functions.output: every row matching control_type for the exact dev_type, or the dwelling_house fallback rows when there is no exact match
functions.if_none: returns an empty list when no row matches, so the callers treat it as no-control-available

functions.name: _dcp_value_conflict
functions.input: a DCPControl list, a control_type string and a dev_type string
functions.output: the sorted distinct value_min values when more than one exists (the selector had to choose), otherwise None
functions.if_none: returns None when zero or one distinct value exists, so no spurious conflict gap is raised

values: N/A - no new DB/API values read; operates on the already-fetched DCPControl list passed into compute_constraint_arithmetic.
queries: N/A - no SQL added or changed; the audit that informed this was a separate read-only probe, not part of the runtime path.

break_it.scenario: A tiered control list is passed in a different row order across two runs (DB ORDER BY changes, or re-extraction reorders rows)
break_it.what_happens: previously the selected setback flipped between tiers (last-row-wins), so the same lot could report different buildable areas run to run
break_it.repro: _get_dcp_value([front 9, front 15]) vs _get_dcp_value([front 15, front 9]) — covered by test_selection_is_order_independent
break_it.how: selection now reduces over ALL matching rows with max()/min(), so it is order-independent; the test asserts both orderings return 15.0

break_it.scenario: Conflicting setback values exist but the engine silently presents one as a single certain figure (the original Burwood 15m bug)
break_it.what_happens: a user sees an authoritative-looking setback/footprint built on an arbitrarily-chosen (and possibly mis-extracted) value with no warning
break_it.repro: compute_constraint_arithmetic with front_setback rows 9m and 15m — covered by test_burwood_conflict_uses_conservative_and_flags_gap
break_it.how: _dcp_value_conflict drives a gap listing all differing values and the conservative one used; the engine still picks the largest (smallest buildable) so it never over-reports capacity while the conflict is flagged for verification

break_it.scenario: A cap control (max_site_coverage) has two values and the change wrongly applies the minimum-requirement (max) rule, loosening the cap
break_it.what_happens: the engine would allow MORE site coverage than the tightest cap, over-reporting buildable area
break_it.how: prefer_max branch reduces with min() over value_max, so the tightest cap wins; the test locks 50.0

break_it.scenario: An exact dev_type control is diluted by dwelling_house fallback rows of the same control_type
break_it.what_happens: a secondary_dwelling setback could be mixed with dwelling_house values and mis-resolved
break_it.repro: _get_dcp_value with a dwelling_house front 6m and a secondary_dwelling front 3m, dev_type='secondary_dwelling' — covered by test_exact_dev_type_preferred_over_dwelling_house (expects 3.0)
break_it.how: _matching_controls returns ONLY exact dev_type rows when any exist; the dwelling_house fallback is used solely when there is no exact match

post_merge.db_reset: N/A - no database change; the bad Burwood/camden rows in dcp_setback_controls are a separate data-quality follow-up (the engine now fails safe and flags them, but the rows still need correcting).
post_merge.other_repo: N/A - services-layer logic only; no Trigger.dev/frontend change. The intelligence brief and capacity card consume the same compute_constraint_arithmetic output and gain the conflict gaps automatically.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run the brief for an LGA with conflicting setbacks (e.g. 14 Stanley St, Croydon Park — Burwood front 9/15): the Development Yield card's footprint is now computed from the conservative setback and a Data Gap flags the conflicting front-setback values for verification. Run a single-setback LGA and confirm no conflict gap appears and the value is unchanged.
